bullets.title: SPX near ATHs on low-vol pullback; risk/reward skewed bullish into OPEX
bullets.body: SPX has corrected only ~2% from all-time highs on decelerating volume (3rd down day in 4), with Hedgeye flagging the vol regime as unchanged and the immediate-term risk range as -0.4% downside vs. +2.5% upside to 7,835. OPEX today means the bulk of SPX positioning has already expired; residual gamma concentrated in weeklies and single-stock options. VIX at 15.31 (+4.4%), with financials implied vol spiking to +77% premium vs. 30-day realized—viewed as panic, not regime change.

bullets.title: UBS raises S&P targets to 8,100 (Dec-26) and 8,400 (Jun-27); Citi says buy pre-midterm dips
bullets.body: UBS Global Wealth Management lifted its 2026 year-end S&P 500 target to 8,100 (from 7,900) and introduced a June 2027 target of 8,400, underpinned by $350/$400 EPS forecasts and tech/semi strength. Separately, Citi maintains overweight on equities, recommending adding exposure on pullbacks ahead of midterms, citing supportive earnings revisions, improving liquidity, and few warning signs.

bullets.title: U.S. PMIs blow out: Services at 56.8% (strongest since late 2024), Manufacturing at 53.2%
bullets.body: August flash U.S. S&P PMIs surprised significantly to the upside—services jumped 2.2 ppts to 56.8%, the strongest reading since late 2024, while manufacturing held at 53.2%. Employment expanded in both sectors, Philadelphia Fed survey showed employment and capex forecasts at multi-decade highs, and the Conference Board LEI turned positive for the first time in 4+ years with 9 of 10 components advancing.

bullets.title: S&P 500 earnings momentum at record highs: 69% Q2 revenue beats, 64% Q3 guidance beats
bullets.body: Of 465 S&P 500 companies reporting, 69% beat Q2 revenue expectations and 64% of those issuing Q3 guidance exceeded consensus forecasts—the highest guidance beat share on record. CNBC's Santoli notes market resilience is underpinned by ~15% S&P margins despite tariffs and geopolitical shocks, though valuation may have peaked near 23x forward earnings.

bullets.title: 30-year Treasury near decade highs at 5.23%; Treasury bond buyback plan failing to convince markets
bullets.body: The 30-year yield eased to ~5.23% on Friday after hitting a near 20-year closing high of 5.311% on Monday. BofA warns that sustained 30-year yields above 5% could trigger risk-asset selling, dollar weakness, and increased short bets against AI names. Treasury intervention attempts are proving ineffective, with bond market volatility picking up and 22V flagging Fed policy as too easy (nominal GDP at 6.5% with zero hikes priced).

bullets.title: USD hits new cycle lows post-Treasury intervention; EUR/USD breaks above 1.16
bullets.body: The DXY broke below the 99.175 200-day moving average following Treasury intervention, entering the 2025-2026 trading range with next support at 97.625-97.74. EUR/USD extended its rebound through 1.16 resistance with bullish momentum; 50% retracement target at 1.1703. Hedgeye confirms dollar as its largest short; gold and metals are benefiting—gold targeting $4,800 near-term per technical analysis.

bullets.title: Gold breakout continues; silver base-and-breakout above $50; commodities outperforming semis
bullets.body: Gold weekly MACD turned from oversold with a $4,800 near-term objective; Newmont Mining within 5% of an all-time high. Silver's quarterly chart shows a classic base-and-breakout above $50 resistance with higher targets. Technical ratios (QQQ/GDX, SMH/GDX) are at tops favoring commodities over semiconductors, and the semiconductor index sits 73% above long-term trend on a monthly basis—base case is a retest of July lows near 10,445.

bullets.title: Bitcoin surges to $79K, up 21% WTD; crypto stocks rally 3-9%; trend signal flipped bullish
bullets.body: Bitcoin surpassed $79,000 on Friday, up ~$15K since Monday and +21% week-to-date, driven in part by U.S. government policy signals and broader risk appetite. Crypto-linked equities surged pre-market (BTDR +8.1%, HOOD +5.1%, HUT +3.3%). Hedgeye confirms Bitcoin's TRADE and TREND signals flipped from bearish to bullish; RSI at 84 with prior shorts obliterated.

bullets.title: Semis: Bullish signals returning in MU, MRVL, SNDK ahead of NVDA earnings; positioning less crowded than August lows
bullets.body: MU and MRVL were the largest positive S&P 500 contributors Thursday; SNDK and DRAM signals returned to bullish Trend. Hedgeye moved its long-only account to maximum 30 positions with ~12 longs vs. 1 short in RTA. KOSPI breaking above 7,000 viewed as a potential catalyst for a significant semiconductor move into NVDA earnings. Mizuho notes tech down 4% vs. SPX down 2% this week, but expects NVDA/AVGO earnings to spark semis recovery; positioning feels less extended than August lows.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole key event risk: Fed Chair Warsh expected to offer modest reassurance on policy
bullets.body: TD Securities and market participants expect Fed Chair Warsh to provide modest reassurance at Jackson Hole, with Citi and others flagging the symposium as a potential catalyst for calming bond markets and supporting a tech rebound. 22V flags nominal GDP at 6.5% with 4.1% unemployment as evidence policy is too accommodative; gold acceleration and term premium surge post-payroll confirm markets are pricing inflation risk premium.

bullets.title: Macro backdrop confirmed healthy: capex-led cycle normal; yields not restrictive per PSC Macro
bullets.body: PSC Macro characterizes the current tech capex-led cycle as historically normal (comparable to 1991, 2002, 2010), with solid jobs (low claims, healthy ISM and NFIB), accelerating nominal GDP, and bond yields elevated but not restrictive. The Fed remains accommodative. AI capex investment is described by Bloomberg as the largest capex-driven GDP contribution in history.

bullets.title: Trump's 50% tariffs imminent; Iran sanctions risk Chinese bank targeting; geopolitical escalation
bullets.body: Trump's 50% tariffs were set to take effect just after midnight, with immediate market implications pending. Separately, Washington is preparing tougher Iran sanctions including potential targeting of major Chinese banks (which buy ~90% of Iranian oil exports), risking trade escalation with Beijing. Iran warned of a 'devastating' response.

bullets.title: Eurozone PMI peaking; ECB rate hike risks rising as CPI tracks to 3.3% by October
bullets.body: Eurozone August composite PMI ticked up 0.1 ppt to 52.1%, but PSC Macro's model forecasts it peaking with manufacturing cooling toward 50.8%. CPI models point to 3.3% y/y by October vs. July's 2.9%, well above ECB's 2% target, with markets pricing in at least one more ECB hike. Bund yields at 3.25%, highest since 2011. UK PMI also beat (52.5 composite vs. 51.6 est), with supercore services inflation at its fastest since December.

bullets.title: Oil second weekly gain; Brent pass-through to Euro inflation rapid and asymmetric
bullets.body: Oil prices head for a second weekly gain on sustained U.S.-Iran pressure; WTI at ~$86.88. JPMorgan flags that a 10% Brent rise passes through to Euro fuel prices by 3.4% within two weeks (vs. only 1.2% for a 10% decline), projecting Eurozone headline inflation hitting 3.4% by September and 3.6% if Brent holds at $95/bbl.

bullets.title: AI data center demand escalating: OpenAI secures 10GW Ohio site; political backlash building
bullets.body: OpenAI is securing a 10GW Ohio data center (5GW by 2028) with Nvidia as exclusive chip provider, underscoring accelerating AI infrastructure demand. Pennsylvania's governor has restricted new AI data center permitting, increasing pricing power for existing assets. Enterprise AI agent deployment tripled in 15 months. Growing political backlash against AI data centers ahead of midterm elections flagged as a rising risk.

bullets.title: AT&T cuts Anthropic spend 90%; open-source shift signals enterprise AI cost discipline
bullets.body: AT&T is shifting AI workloads to open-source models, cutting Anthropic spending by up to 90%. This follows a broader pattern of enterprise cost discipline in AI deployment even as infrastructure capex accelerates. Separately, 22V flags Mistral's pivot from frontier model training to regional compute hosting as Europe's effective exit from the AI development race.

bullets.title: Rotation signal: Tech/semis underperforming; 'Experiences' pocket and non-AI cyclicals broadening
bullets.body: GS TMT desk flags AI high-flyers (COHR, ALAB, LITE, STX) compressing P/E from ~70x to ~40x in 45 days despite rising estimates. The 'Experiences' pocket (EXPE, UBER, DIS, ABNB) is broadening with multi-week winning streaks. European cyclicals down 7 consecutive sessions. Morgan Stanley's non-AI best ideas webcast focuses on MCK, MSI, and M as idiosyncratic alternatives to AI-dominated positioning.

bullets.title: Global fund manager survey 3rd most bullish since 2022; analyst optimism at dot-com-era levels
bullets.body: BofA's August global fund manager survey shows equity allocations at their highest since November 2021, ranking as the 3rd most bullish survey since 2022. Separately, a cited analyst notes sell-side optimism is at levels only previously seen prior to the dot-com bubble and in post-recession recoveries—a cautionary sentiment signal for contrarians.

bullets.title: Hedgeye ETF re-rank: QTUM +11, VYM +9, VCSH +6 lead; FXY and FXE worst movers
bullets.body: McCullough's daily ETF re-rank shows quantum computing (QTUM), value dividend (VYM), and short-duration credit (VCSH) leading on the week. He added HYG at minimum allocation, sold all ROBO positions, and trimmed several positions. FXY (-15) and FXE (-12) are the worst movers, consistent with the broader long-Euro/Yen, short-Dollar macro positioning.

bullets.title: 22V flags TPS worker shock as NFP headwind; structural ~2% U.S. growth speed limit
bullets.body: 22V estimates 400-500K TPS workers losing work authorization from late July through early October will create a temporary but meaningful NFP headwind, with breakeven NFP growth already near ~25k/month. Separately, 22V sees a structural ~2% U.S. growth speed limit driven by collapsed population growth, making Treasury yield curve intervention attempts largely irrelevant to real economy constraints.
